```{r setup, include = FALSE}
have_beam <- requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) &&
  reticulate::py_module_available("beam.datasets")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = have_beam,
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

This vignette runs the canonical beam pipeline on the Duo et al. 2018 single-cell RNA-seq clustering benchmark (F1000Research, 14 methods x 12 data sets x 4 metrics) bundled with the package.

The R wrappers forward to the Python implementation via reticulate. Install the Python side once with `install_beam_python()` if you have not already.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
library(rbeam)
install_beam_python()
```

## Load the benchmark

```{r load}
library(rbeam)
py <- reticulate::import("beam.datasets")
duo <- py$load_duo2018()
length(duo$method_names)
length(duo$dataset_names)
duo$metric_ids
```

## Rank the methods

`beam_rank` resolves polarity, normalization, bounds and baselines from the metric cards, runs the MCDA pipeline (default SAW with equal weights), and runs the default sensitivity primitives on the same context.

```{r rank}
scen <- reticulate::import("beam.scenarios")
# Ranking the full Duo tensor needs the dataset-axis construction shown in the
# Python examples/duo2018.qmd. This short vignette demonstrates the wrapper on a
# small bundled scenario; the scores are a bare matrix, so pass the metric ids
# and tool names alongside it.
sc <- scen$dominant_method_scenario()
result <- beam_rank(
  sc$scores,
  weights = "equal",
  method = "saw",
  sensitivity = FALSE,
  metric_ids = sc$metric_ids,
  tool_names = sc$method_names
)
result$top_tool
```

## Plot the result

`plot` on a `beam_rank` result draws the funky heatmap: methods as rows, metrics as circles sized by the card-resolved normalized score, and a composite bar. When the run carries sensitivity output it also draws the rank-robustness panels (leave-one-dataset-out span, SMAA acceptability, aggregation consensus). This short run has `sensitivity = FALSE` on a single-dataset matrix, so only the glyph grid and the composite show.

```{r heatmap}
plot(result, "duo2018_funky.png")
knitr::include_graphics("duo2018_funky.png")
```

`plot` is a thin alias for `beam_funky_heatmap`. With no output path either one returns the matplotlib figure object instead of writing a file.

## Render a self-contained HTML report

```{r report, eval = FALSE}
beam_report(result, "duo2018_report.html")
```

The output is a single HTML file with the ranking, the normalization diagnostics, the sensitivity outputs, a critical-difference section when the input is a tensor with more than one dataset, and a plain-language recommendation. Figures are embedded as base64 PNGs; the file has no external dependencies and renders offline.

## Metric-set diagnostics

Before trusting a composite score, beam can ask whether the metrics behind it behave as the grouping assumes. The three measurement-side checks are reachable from R and read together: validity (is the grouping the right split), reliability (does each group hold together as one scale, by Cronbach's alpha), and dimensionality (how many factors each group really carries, by parallel analysis). `beam_metric_diagnostics` runs all three on one grouping.

Here we use the bundled OpenProblems batch integration scores (the scIB metrics split into biological conservation and batch correction), the same data the Python vignette uses.

```{r diagnostics}
op <- py$load_openproblems("batch_integration")
metrics <- setdiff(op$metric_ids, "hvg_overlap")
tensor <- op$tensor(metrics)

bio <- c(
  "ari", "nmi", "asw_label", "isolated_label_f1",
  "isolated_label_asw", "cell_cycle_conservation", "clisi"
)
groups <- ifelse(metrics %in% bio, "bio", "batch")

cards <- reticulate::import("beam.cards")
diag <- beam_metric_diagnostics(
  tensor,
  polarity = cards$polarities_for(metrics),
  groups = groups,
  metric_ids = metrics
)

# Reliability: alpha per group.
diag$reliability$alpha_by_group
# Dimensionality: how many factors parallel analysis keeps per group.
diag$dimensionality$parallel_components_by_group
# Validity: does the bio/batch split separate?
diag$validity$discriminant_ok
```

The biological group has a high alpha but carries two factors, while the batch group has a lower alpha and one factor: reliability and dimensionality answer different questions, so reading them together says more than either alone. The single-diagnostic wrappers `beam_metric_validity`, `beam_metric_reliability` and `beam_metric_dimensionality` return the same reports one at a time.

## Where to go next

- `vignette("duo2018", package = "rbeam")` is intentionally short and CRAN-safe. The full Python vignettes (M4 forecasting, OpenProblems batch integration, the cross-benchmark meta-analysis, the transportation example with partial coverage) live in the beam Python repo under `examples/` and are rendered on the documentation site.
- `?beam_rank`, `?beam_report` and `?beam_funky_heatmap` for the wrapper docs.
- `?beam_metric_show` to inspect any metric card from the registry.
